ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, points D, C, B are on the same horizontal straight line, with C located between D and B; line segments are drawn from A to D, C, B respectively. Segments AD and DC both have the same double tick marks, indicating AD ≅ DC. Angle ∠ADC is labeled 92°. What is asked for is ∠ACB. Reasoning: Because AD ≅ DC, triangle ADC is an isosceles triangle, and its base angles ∠DAC and ∠ACD are equal. Given ∠ADC = 92°, so ∠DAC + ∠ACD = 180° - 92° = 88°, therefore ∠ACD = 88° ÷ 2 = 44°. Also because CD and CB are opposite rays on the same straight line, ∠ACD and ∠ACB form a linear pair, with sum 180°. Therefore m∠ACB = 180° - 44° = 136°.

Because CD and CB are opposite rays on the same straight line, ∠ACD and ∠ACB form a linear pair, so m∠ACB = 180° - 44° = 136°.
